Animal Flashcards for Preschoolers

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Say the name, then make the sound

    The pair is the whole lesson: “dog… woof!” Say both in one breath, then let your child take over the sound. The animal name gets the quiet word; the sound gets the fun one.

  2. 02

    Press play, then answer it yourself

    On the pages with a play button, listen to the real animal once — then answer it in your own voice. Your child will copy you long before they copy the speaker.

  3. 03

    Play the guessing game backwards

    Once three or four cards feel easy, your child holds the cards and makes a sound; you point at the animal it belongs to. Getting one wrong on purpose keeps the game alive for weeks.

  4. 04

    Take one card on the road

    Tape the dog card by the window or the bird card by the door. Every real woof or tweet you spot together is one more quiet repetition — and repetitions are what make animal words stick.

      Dog Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The dog says woof — most children meet this sound first, from storybooks to the neighbour’s puppy. On this card the word dog sits under a happy brown puppy, and the woof is ready to play the moment you press play.

      Teaching tips

      What this animal card does

      Turns the household woof into a real word, printed and pointed at daily.

      Move like it

      Shake like a wet dog — whole-body wiggle from head to hands, twice.

      What kids learn from it

      Points, names and greets — three household skills riding one word.

      Print tips

      Card stock, full size — this one gets carried to the park.

      Tip for today

      Keep it near the front door; visitors arrive with four legs here.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Dog lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ANIMALS & THEIR SOUNDS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Cat Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A soft meee-ow is one of the first sounds children make up themselves. This card pairs the word cat with an orange kitten, and the meow recording is one tap away.

      Teaching tips

      What this animal card does

      Gives the morning stretch a name and the hallway cat a greeting.

      Move like it

      Do the long cat stretch — arched back, toes spread, one enormous yawn.

      What kids learn from it

      Daily stretches become vocabulary worth showing off.

      Print tips

      Ordinary paper is fine; cats are low-drama guests.

      Tip for today

      Whisper the word sometimes — cats approve of quiet talk.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Cat lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ANIMALS & THEIR SOUNDS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Cow Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Moo is a whole-body sound: open wide, let it rumble, make it last. The word cow sits under a spotted farm cow, and a real moo is ready to hear together.

      Teaching tips

      What this animal card does

      Puts a friendly name on the spotted giant of every farm book.

      Move like it

      Chew like a cow — slow, sideways jaw circles, completely unhurried, very satisfying.

      What kids learn from it

      Slow jaws meet slow words; patience gets a mascot.

      Print tips

      Print two to a page; the herd likes company.

      Tip for today

      Break the word in half — c-ow — slowly, then all together.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Cow lesson on the Learning Path.

      Sheep Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The sheep’s baa wobbles at the end — baa-aa-aa — which makes it irresistible to copy. This card shows a fluffy white sheep with the word sheep, and the baa is one tap away.

      Teaching tips

      What this animal card does

      Names the fluffiest card in the set and the woolly jumper on the rack.

      Move like it

      Graze across the rug, head low, nibbling imaginary grass with tiny sidesteps.

      What kids learn from it

      Soft and fluffy become describing words with a woolly example attached.

      Print tips

      Matte paper suits sheep best — no glare on all that fluff.

      Tip for today

      Count the sheep at bedtime; the card makes a fine first sheep.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Sheep lesson on the Learning Path.

      Duck Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Quack is a short, sharp, funny sound — three waddles and one quack is already a game. The word duck sits under a yellow duckling, ready for the kitchen table.

      Teaching tips

      What this animal card does

      Gives your child the word for the bird that answers itself twice.

      Move like it

      Sit down and paddle your feet fast — calm top half, busy hidden legs.

      What kids learn from it

      One short word covers a bird, a swim and a waddle.

      Print tips

      Laminate this one; ducklings splash, even printed ones.

      Tip for today

      Say quack flat and bored once; the giggles restart the whole game.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Duck lesson on the Learning Path.

      Chicken Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The hen clucks all day — bok, bok, bok — a busy sound for busy little people. This card pairs the word chicken with a white hen, and the cluck recording plays on tap.

      Teaching tips

      What this animal card does

      Names the bird your child already meets at breakfast, in books and at the farm.

      Move like it

      Scratch the floor with one foot, stand tall, scan the room, repeat.

      What kids learn from it

      Constant motion gets a word, which every busy parent secretly needs.

      Print tips

      Print it beside the egg cup; hens and breakfast belong together.

      Tip for today

      Keep it clucky and light; nobody needs the lifecycle lecture today.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Chicken lesson on the Learning Path.

      Horse Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A horse’s neigh starts high and slides down — a sound children love to ride. The word horse sits under a tall brown horse, with the whinny ready to hear.

      Teaching tips

      What this animal card does

      Brings the tallest animal in the set down to table height, word attached.

      Move like it

      Toss an imaginary mane — big proud head-flicks, twice each side, very proud.

      What kids learn from it

      Height words grow from here — tall, taller, and eventually giraffe.

      Print tips

      Full-page print suits this one; horses hate being cropped.

      Tip for today

      Say it long and low; horrrse has its own gait.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Horse lesson on the Learning Path.

      Pig Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Oink comes straight from the nose — sniff, sniff, snort! This card shows a smiling pink pig with the word pig, and a real pig grunt plays on tap.

      Teaching tips

      What this animal card does

      Owns the word for the pink card everybody grabs first — usually this one.

      Move like it

      Flop sideways onto the cushions like a pig into a perfect puddle, then rise, delighted.

      What kids learn from it

      Messy enthusiasm gets a word, which keeps enthusiasm printable.

      Print tips

      Thick card recommended; pigs survive enthusiastic handling.

      Tip for today

      Oink optional — the word alone is a perfectly respectable pig impression.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Pig lesson on the Learning Path.

      Lion Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Every child has a roar in them — this one starts soft and ends loud. The word lion sits under a shaggy-maned lion, and a real roar plays at the press of a button.

      Teaching tips

      What this animal card does

      Delivers the most requested sound in any house, printed and ready for repeat performances.

      Move like it

      Stalk the hallway in slow motion, then pounce on whatever squeaks.

      What kids learn from it

      Volume control starts as a joke and lands as a skill.

      Print tips

      Print at full size; the mane reads better with room to spread.

      Tip for today

      One roar per request keeps the game royal instead of relentless.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Lion lesson on the Learning Path.

      Elephant Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The elephant’s trumpet is the silliest sound in the set: Pbbbfft! The word elephant sits under a gray giant, and the arm-trunk game is waiting in the say-it-together box.

      Teaching tips

      What this animal card does

      Carries the biggest body in the set and a word to match.

      Move like it

      Flap elbow ears while lumbering — three slow, floor-considering steps, then a turn.

      What kids learn from it

      Big and heavy find their word, and size talk begins.

      Print tips

      Grey ink optional; the outline carries the shape if the printer economises.

      Tip for today

      Slow everything down to elephant speed and the copying gets easier.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Elephant lesson on the Learning Path.

      Frog Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ribbit is a bouncy little sound made for hopping: one hop, one ribbit. The word frog sits under a bright green frog, ready for the kitchen table.

      Teaching tips

      What this animal card does

      Puts a spring in the word and a crouch in the living room.

      Move like it

      Snap one hand shut mid-air, frog-style — breakfast caught, no fork required.

      What kids learn from it

      Sharp eyes, quicker hands, and the attention span of a hunter.

      Print tips

      Two copies print well — frogs multiply, as frogs do.

      Tip for today

      Snap at each other's imaginary flies; turn-taking comes free.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Frog lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ANIMALS & THEIR SOUNDS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Bird Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Tweet, tweet — the smallest voice on the cards, and the one your child can hear for real outside the window. The word bird sits under a little bluebird, with a real tweet on tap.

      Teaching tips

      What this animal card does

      Names the smallest card resident and every feathered visitor to the garden.

      Move like it

      Tilt one head at the window, suspicious and thorough, then hop twice sideways.

      What kids learn from it

      Watching quietly is a real skill, and this card starts it.

      Print tips

      Small sizes print crisply; this is the set's most pocketable resident.

      Tip for today

      One bird word per window is plenty; the sparrows will wait.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Bird lesson on the Learning Path.
